lines.text: You found a function in the game. To understand it, or to call it yourself, you need to know one thing: where do its arguments go?
In thirty-two bit code, they go on the stack. Pushed right to left, so the first argument ends up on top.
Inside the function, E B P plus eight is the first argument. Plus twelve is the second. And E B P minus four is a local variable.

Who cleans the stack afterwards? In the C convention, the caller does: you see an add to E S P right after the call. In the Windows convention, the function does: it ends with a return that pops its own arguments.
C plus plus methods add one more thing: the object itself travels in E C X. Find what loads E C X before a call, and you have found the player.
Sixty-four bit Windows has one rule for everyone. The first four arguments ride in registers: R C X, R D X, R eight and R nine. The result comes back in R A X.
Stack or registers. Once you know where the arguments go, you can read any call.
